title: Norway's oil and gas giant fights an ongoing cyber attack
plain: Equinor, Europe's biggest gas supplier, says hackers are inside some of its office computer systems. Oil and gas production hasn't been affected, and so far there's no sign that data was taken.
tech: Ongoing intrusion against 'certain IT systems'; disruption to internal applications, with Reuters' source saying internal email was down. No access vector, malware family or ransomware confirmed. Production and OT reported unaffected. NSM assisting; Havtil and PST informed.

title: Australian supermarket Coles looks into a cyber attack
plain: Coles says it's dealing with a cyber attack. Shops are open as normal, and it has found no sign that customer, staff or supplier details were taken.
tech: Incident disclosed 16 Nov via ASX statement; discovery date and access method not disclosed. Minor Liquorland click-and-collect disruption; Flybuys, Coles Plus and stores unaffected. No group has claimed it. Working with the Australian Cyber Security Centre.

title: Japanese furniture chain Nitori leaks millions of member records
plain: Someone got into a Nitori computer system and took members' names, addresses, phone numbers and order details. About 37.6 million records are involved.
tech: Unauthorised access to a system on the company network. Exposed: names, emails, postal addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, gender, corporate contacts and order history (about 37.62 million records). Access vector not disclosed.

title: Gang claims Maersk hack and demands $5 million
plain: A criminal gang says it broke into an old Maersk system and stole delivery drivers' details. Maersk says no sensitive data has come out.
tech: WhiteArmor ransomware group claims access to a legacy system inherited through an acquisition, alleging about 30,000 driver records with plaintext passwords plus 27,842 device logs (phone numbers, emails, IMEIs); $5m demand. Maersk disputes that sensitive data was disclosed.

title: Hotel group Wyndham's app had a password baked into it
plain: Wyndham's Android app contained a hidden password that opened a customer database. Names, emails and member numbers were exposed.
tech: Hard-coded credential in the Wyndham Android app granted access to a Salesforce-hosted database with 'millions of entries': customer names, emails, rewards member numbers, login tokens and internal files. Wyndham has about 129 million rewards members; the number affected is unknown.

title: Norway's aid agency loses data on every grant portal user
plain: Hackers got into Norad's grant website using 27 staff or user accounts and took the names and emails of all 20,614 people registered there.
tech: Detected 30 Oct 2026. 27 accounts compromised and used to access the grant portal; names and email addresses of all 20,614 users across 12,511 organisations taken, and at least three grant applications misdirected. How the accounts were compromised is not disclosed. Outside responders engaged.
